lead: Between Sants and the Zona Franca, with Can Batlló, a former factory turned into a community space.
text: In 1801 it was a neighbourhood of a single street, the old Roman Via Augusta that linked Barcelona with Tarragona. From 1857 it was one of the four neighbourhoods of the independent municipality of Sants, annexed to Barcelona in 1897. The great change came in 1880 with the Can Batlló textile factory, now being transformed: 170,000 m² of parks, public facilities and housing, in which the main hall will be preserved. The first phase of the Can Batlló park opened in November 2024, with 29,000 m² and 486 new trees, and according to the municipal action plan, updated in April 2026, the transformation of the site is 80% complete, with the Escola de Mitjans Audiovisuals already built.

It is a residential, well-connected area, halfway between the centre of Sants and L'Hospitalet. In the 1970s the neighbourhood movement opposed the Ronda del Mig, and among its victories are the Placeta de la Pelleria, the partial covering of the ring road and the primary healthcare centre. With 21,153 inhabitants in 0.57 km², it has a density of 36,981 inhabitants/km², and its average sale price, 3,855 €/m², is below that of Sants. If you are selling, the average sale price is practically in line with the Sants-Montjuïc average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 308,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Sants-Montjuïc (6th of 8 by price). If you are investing, the average rent (1,186 €/month) is 18% above the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Blocks of flats and buildings from various periods, on streets with local shops.
